facts.fact: The StackAdapt blog post 'How to optimize for high landing page conversion rates' was published on March 18, 2021.
The article defines cost per engagement (CPE) as the total ad cost of a campaign divided by the total number of engagement actions with an ad.
facts.quote: CPE is calculated by dividing the total ad cost of your campaign by the total number of engagement actions with an ad.

facts.fact: The article defines conversion rate (CVR) as the number of conversions divided by the total number of visitors who clicked through to the landing page.
facts.quote: CVR is calculated by dividing the number of conversions by the total number of visitors who clicked through to your landing page.

facts.fact: The article states that sales landing pages tend to be longer than lead capture landing pages and include elements such as social proof, FAQ, and sometimes case studies.
facts.quote: Compared to a lead capture landing page, sales landing pages tend to be longer and include elements like social proof, FAQ, and sometimes case studies.

facts.fact: The article describes a lead capture landing page as one that offers users something in return for their email address or other information.
facts.quote: A lead capture page offers users something in return for their email address or other information.

facts.fact: The article defines 'above the fold' as the content of a web page that is immediately visible when the page first loads.
facts.quote: The term “above the fold” refers to the content of a web page that is immediately visible when a page first loads.

facts.fact: The article states it is best practice to have just one call to action on a landing page, unless multiple CTAs are tracked differently.
facts.quote: it’s best practice to have just one CTA, because competing CTAs can be confusing for the user

facts.fact: The article states that enabling StackAdapt's engagement pixel helps advertisers track metrics such as bounce rate on their landing page.
facts.quote: enabling StackAdapt’s engagement pixel will help you track metrics like bounce rate.

facts.fact: The article gives 'Learn More,' 'Shop Now,' and 'Sign Up' as examples of effective CTAs because they are short and to the point.
facts.quote: CTAs like “Learn More,” “Shop Now,” and “Sign Up” are effective because they are short and to the point.
